firms.name: Invesco Real Estate
firms.quote: $87.2 billion in real estate assets under management
firms.notes: Real estate arm of Invesco Ltd, based in Dallas since 1983; AUM and headcount are from a Feb 2026 release using June 30, 2025 data (601 employees, 21 regional offices worldwide). Dallas office was long at 2001 Ross Ave, Suite 3400 (Trammell Crow Center), but DMN reported in Mar 2024 a planned move to The Union, 2300 N. Field St., so the current address is unconfirmed. Property types and strategies listed are general to the platform, not individually verified; DFW projects not researched.

firms.name: Comerica
firms.notes: Bank figure is a balance-sheet total, not real estate AUM. At 31 Dec 2024 Comerica held $3.68B of real estate construction loans and $14.49B of commercial mortgage loans (the latter includes owner-occupied loans, so not all is investor CRE); management said its CRE strategy centres on construction lending. Fifth Third completed its acquisition of Comerica on 2 Feb 2026 (combined ~$294B assets), so Comerica is no longer an independent Dallas-headquartered company; the founding year 1849 (Detroit) is from general knowledge and should be checked.

firms.name: Lument
firms.quote: maintain a servicing portfolio exceeding $56.5 billion
projects: $123.6M CMBS refinancing of a Dallas multifamily portfolio
firms.notes: Scale is a loan servicing portfolio (Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, HUD/FHA and bridge loans), not loans owned; company calls itself the #1 FHA MAP lender by loan count. Lument is a subsidiary of ORIX Corporation USA (Dallas-based parent); the brand was formed in Oct 2020 by combining Hunt Real Estate Capital, Lancaster Pollard and RED Capital Group. No Lument-only headcount was found: ORIX USA and its subsidiaries 'employ over 2,000 professionals' (~2,100 as of 31 Mar 2026). Its main office is listed in New York, with a significant Dallas office whose current address is unconfirmed (2001 Ross Ave vs. 700 N. Pearl St reported in different sources).

firms.name: ORIX USA
firms.notes: Scale metric is labelled 'assets and commitments' by ORIX (closest to AUM; includes balance-sheet assets) across all of ORIX USA (private credit, real estate, private equity), not real estate alone; the homepage showed $40.1B later in 2026. Real estate arms are Lument (multifamily, affordable, seniors, healthcare lending) and Boston Financial (LIHTC); Dallas has been joint HQ with New York since 2017 (US HQ moved to Dallas 2004). Founded 1981 per secondary sources; ~2,100 employees firmwide, ~300 moved into the Dallas office in 2020.

firms.name: Crow Holdings

fund.name: Crow Holdings Realty Partners X (Tenth U.S. Diversified Value-Add Real Estate Fund)

firms.notes: Founded 1948 when Trammell Crow built his first Dallas warehouse. Site reports $36B AUM as of 30 Jun 2026, of which Crow Holdings Capital is $21.5B (incl. $15.7B regulatory AUM); Bisnow (2 Sep 2026) reported $35B and that Fund XI (target $3.25B per SEC filing) had raised nearly $1.1B with no final close found. Preliminary $33B figure was outdated. Employee count is a third-party estimate (Revelio Labs); other estimates range widely. Hilton Anatole and Trammell Crow Center are historical Crow projects, not necessarily current holdings.

firms.name: Texas Capital
firms.notes: Texas Capital Bancshares (NASDAQ: TCBI) is a full-service commercial bank, not a dedicated real estate lender; total assets are bank-wide and loans held for investment were $18.64B at 30 Sep 2026 (CRE balance not broken out in the earnings release). Incorporated 1996, began banking operations 1998, per its 10-K; 10-K quote: 'At December 31, 2025, the Company had 1,785 employees, nearly all of whom are full time.'

firms.name: Trammell Crow Company
firms.quote: nearly $30 billion of projects in process or its pipeline
firms.notes: Dallas-headquartered developer, a wholly owned subsidiary of CBRE (CBRE is already on the known list, so dedupe at your discretion); High Street Residential is its multifamily arm. DFW unit oversees about $2.5B under way plus $1B pipeline (Dec 2025). Founding year 1948 from general knowledge, unverified here.

firms.name: JPI
firms.quote: delivering over 117,000 homes with a total value of $26 billion
firms.notes: Irving-based multifamily developer acquired by Sumitomo Forestry in 2023. Per its own releases it started 17 projects (6,372 homes, $2.2B development value) in 2025 and ranked No. 2 on NMHC's 2026 Top 25 Developers list. The $26B is cumulative value of everything delivered since 1989 (a JPI release, quoted via search summary).

firms.name: CyrusOne
firms.notes: Data center developer-operator taken private by KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners in 2022 in a deal valued at about $15 billion (the scale figure is that take-private value, not AUM). March 2026 release says it operates over 60 data centers across the U.S., Europe and Japan, and upsized loan facilities to $8.0 billion.

firms.name: PlainsCapital
firms.notes: PlainsCapital Bank (FDIC cert 17491) is the bank subsidiary of Hilltop Holdings (Hilltop total assets $15.8B at 31 Dec 2025). Figures are bank balance-sheet totals, not real estate AUM. Call report 30 Jun 2026: real estate loans $7.65B of $9.27B gross loans, of which nonfarm nonresidential $3.34B, construction/land $0.98B, multifamily $0.36B (about $4.69B commercial real estate combined). Founding date is the FDIC establishment date.

firms.name: Canyon Partners Real Estate
firms.quote: approximately $12.6 billion total capitalization of real estate assets

fund.name: Canyon US Real Estate Debt Fund III

firms.notes: Real estate arm of Dallas-based alternative manager Canyon Partners; has deployed $4 billion of investor capital. Fund III invests in senior and subordinate real estate debt; roughly double its $650M predecessor. The parent is a multi-strategy credit manager, not solely real estate.

firms.name: Knightvest Capital
firms.notes: Self-described vertically integrated multifamily investor/manager: 'Acquired over 67,000 units with a current portfolio of over 35,000+ units'. The $12B is cumulative capital invested, not AUM. The site's '100 dedicated management professionals' probably excludes on-site property staff, so firmwide headcount may be higher.

firms.name: KDC
firms.quote: 37 million square feet of high-performance real estate valued at over $11 billion
firms.notes: Corporate build-to-suit and campus developer; site says 'Since 1989' and 'Headquartered in Dallas' (Steve Van Amburgh now executive chairman). The $11B is the cumulative value of everything KDC has developed (37M sq ft, 40+ markets), not AUM; earlier reports gave $3.7B/27M sq ft and $9B/36M sq ft, so figures depend on date and scope. HQ address is from third-party listings and a TDLR filing, not the company site; employee band is unverified (ZoomInfo says 201-500).

firms.name: Granite Properties
firms.quote: has executed $10.3 billion in CRE transactions
firms.notes: July 2025 brochure: owns and operates 11 million sq ft of office space, $10.3B of CRE transactions executed, 30 million sq ft developed; since 2021 deployed $2.3B ($700M acquisitions, $1.6B development) funded with $1.2B of partner equity. Founded 1991 per its 2011 20th-anniversary release. Employee figure is dated (Great Place to Work, 2021); other directories give 51-200 or 209.

firms.name: Sealy & Company
firms.notes: Fourth-generation family industrial investor. HQ is ambiguous: releases cite corporate offices in Dallas and Shreveport, LA, and some press calls it Shreveport-based; include with that caveat. Employees shown as '125+'. Founding year not stated ('80+ Years of Experience').

firms.name: Pacific Elm Properties
firms.quote: over $6 billion in real estate acquisition and/or development transactions
firms.notes: Company site: 'six Class A towers totaling 4.4 million square feet' plus land in Dallas and Raleigh; the $6B transactions figure may include principals' prior deals. Founder Jonas Woods handed the CEO role to Billy Prewitt in Sept 2025 to lead spinoff 3-O Real Estate Partners (its $4B pipeline belongs to 3-O, not Pacific Elm). Bisnow gives a 2021 founding year, which may reflect a reorganization rather than first activity; press also reported foreclosure on One Dallas Center a year after losing Comerica Bank Tower.

firms.name: S2 Capital
firms.address: 2801 N. Harwood Street, Suite 1800, Dallas, TX 75201
firms.quote: $6 billion of multifamily assets under management

fund.name: S2 Real Estate Fund II LP

firms.notes: Multifamily syndicator/fund manager led by CEO Scott Everett. The $6B AUM is from Sept 2022 (Fund I closed at its $400M hard cap); no newer AUM found, and the preliminary '$5.3B property AUM' could not be sourced. Dallas Innovates (Jul 2025) says Fund II's $373M exceeded Fund I's commitments, which conflicts with Fund I's reported $400M hard cap. The Real Deal reported in Jun 2025 that S2 faced foreclosure on an Arlington complex. Employee estimates conflict (ZoomInfo 501-1,000; Prospeo 201-500); the registered adviser S2 Fund Manager LLC reports ~42-45 staff.

firms.name: Stonelake Capital Partners
firms.quote: owns over $6.0 billion of commercial real estate in Sunbelt Markets
projects: 2626 McKinney Avenue (17-story Uptown office tower, under construction)
firms.notes: Homepage figure is undated (read Nov 2026) and states owned real estate, not AUM; a 2023 firm document gave ~$4.5B AUM. HQ listed at 100 Crescent Court, but a lease record shows a move to 23Springs (2323 Cedar Springs Rd, 9th floor) closing March 2026 - unconfirmed; PERE also calls the firm Austin-based. Fund VIII closed 30 Sep 2026 at a $1B hard cap; Fund VII closed 2023 at $746M.

firms.name: StreetLights Residential
projects: Viridian: The Jackson and The Louise (Arlington)
Park Lane tower with Mitsui Fudosan (Dallas)
firms.notes: Dallas-based design-focused multifamily developer with in-house architecture and construction affiliates; website lists 16.4K multifamily units. The site labels $5.8B as 'Capitalization' without defining it, so the metric label is approximate.

firms.name: Cypress Equities
firms.address: 8144 Walnut Hill Lane, Suite 1200, Dallas, TX 75231
firms.notes: Dallas retail and mixed-use developer; website cites $2.2 billion of total invested equity and over 20 million square feet of retail, office, residential, automotive, hotel and industrial projects. Ownership/parent not verified here.

firms.name: Crescent Real Estate
firms.address: 3230 Camp Bowie Blvd, Suite 500, Fort Worth, TX 76107
firms.notes: Scale is SEC Form ADV regulatory AUM (CRD 158397); the company's own site claims '$17B+ Investments' measured by original acquisition price (Dec 2025), and The Real Deal cited $4.3B AUM at end of 2024. GPIF IV closed 31 Dec 2025 at ~$241.5M (company site says $240M of GP fund commitments). Founding year is ambiguous: The Real Deal says 1987 (John Goff and Richard Rainwater); the current LLC succeeded the REIT Crescent Real Estate Equities.

firms.name: TriGate Capital
firms.notes: Dallas fund manager; website cites $1.5B cumulative equity invested and 9,000 residential lots and units. A January 2025 SEC filing showed it seeking $700M for a fifth fund (status of that close not confirmed); Fund III size per secondary summaries of PERE coverage.

firms.name: Westdale
firms.quote: our multifamily management portfolio exceeds $3 billion
firms.notes: Founded 1991 in Dallas by Joe Beard, originally affiliated with a Canadian family-office partner; distinct from Toronto-based Westdale Properties. The $3B figure is a self-described multifamily management portfolio (180 communities, ~45,000 units, undated); NMHC's 2025 Top 50 Owners reportedly lists 31,631 units owned. Preliminary '$5B capital base' and 1,200 employees could not be confirmed from an accessible primary source (westdale.com and LoopNet return 403); employee estimates range 546-1,100. Several Deep Ellum assets may since have been sold; verify current ownership.

firms.name: NewcrestImage
firms.notes: Grapevine-based hotel developer, owner and operator; website cites 277 hotel transactions. Owned-hotel counts in press vary (22 vs 28) by date.

firms.name: Presidium
projects: Presidium Valley View (344 units, Farmers Branch)
firms.notes: Company site cites a '23-year operating history' but gives no founding year (a Fort Worth Chamber listing for 'Presidium Development' says 2002, possibly a different entity). Markets per site: Dallas, Austin, Jacksonville and Portland, Maine. The 250 employees figure is 'US Employees' from the 2026 Top Workplaces DFW listing and likely includes property-management staff. HQ address from TDLR filings (Citymark building).

firms.name: The Milestone Group

fund.name: Milestone Real Estate Investors VI LP

ADV employee count excludes clerical staff and covers the adviser entity. Offices in Dallas, Boca Raton and Atlanta; Fund VI closed Sep 2025 at its $1.1B hard cap targeting the Sunbelt and Mid-Atlantic. No specific DFW properties confirmed in this pass.

firms.name: Todd Interests
firms.quote: more than 1.5 billion dollars of real estate property

Morgan Asset Management (Dec 2025) and that Starwood Property Trust took back The National at foreclosure (Feb 2026), so the current portfolio is smaller than the project list suggests. Office at 400 N. Ervay per Dallas Innovates; suite number unconfirmed by the company.

firms.name: CONTI Capital
firms.quote: over $1.25 billion in transactions to date
firms.notes: Dallas real estate investment firm raising from accredited investors under Rule 506(c). The $150M is Fund IV's 2021 target, not a confirmed close. Website URL not verified.

firms.name: HN Capital Partners
projects: Dallas Design District portfolio (with McCourt Partners)
firms.notes: Founded and led by Vipin Nambiar; acquisitions record begins 2017 but no founding year found. Site reports over $1.2B acquired and over 2.2M sq ft developed area owned; D CEO (Nov 2024) quoted Nambiar saying the firm 'recently ticked over $1 billion in assets'. Ownership stakes in named hotels may be partial/joint-venture.

firms.name: Caddis

Founding year 2008 is from press coverage (Dallas Morning News), not the company site.

firms.name: HALL Structured Finance

firms.notes: Private lending division of HALL Group; provides non-recourse first-lien construction loans, bridge loans and preferred equity of $20M-$200M, mainly hotel and multifamily. LinkedIn reportedly gives a 2002 founding date (unverified). Several similarly named entities (Altera Rayzor Ranch apartments in Denton, Altera Legacy Oaks in San Antonio, Alterra Development) appear unrelated; geography beyond Texas not confirmed.

firms.name: Revere Capital
firms.address: 5910 N. Central Expressway, Suite 1600, Dallas, TX 75206
firms.notes: Dallas private lender doing lower middle-market CRE bridge loans plus asset-backed specialty finance (so not purely real estate). The $350M fund was announced (target) in 2017; final size not confirmed.

firms.name: Leon Capital Group
projects: Leon Multifamily apartment project, Mansfield ($33.5M financing)
firms.notes: Scale and employees are from the SEC Form ADV of Leon Capital Management, LLC (CRD 332987), the group's registered-adviser arm only; they understate the diversified holding company (real estate plus healthcare, financial services, technology). Other figures in circulation are unverified: a third-party profile says ~$3B in assets and company copy says it has overseen 'more than $10 billion in private capital'. Founder/CEO Fernando De Leon; 2006 founding year comes from a Wikipedia-derived page and is not confirmed by the company.

firms.name: Velocis
firms.quote: closed on a new $172M investment fund
firms.notes: Dallas real estate manager; Fund I closed at $135M and Fund II at $270M. Fund III buys LP interests in real estate funds on the secondary market.

firms.name: Move It Self Storage
firms.quote: $25 million pool of cash from its first-ever equity fund
firms.notes: Dallas-based self-storage owner/operator (Move It Management). In 2024 it had 90 locations in six states and planned about $100 million of mostly ground-up spending backed by the $25M fund. Fund figures are from SpareFoot as relayed by search (page itself blocked automated fetch); website not verified.

firms.name: Ashford Hospitality Trust
firms.notes: Upscale full-service hotel REIT (NYSE: AHT) externally advised by Dallas-based Ashford Inc. Its FY2025 10-K disclosed substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern. Founding year 2003 (IPO) from general knowledge, unverified here.

firms.name: Bandera Ventures
firms.notes: Founded 2003 by Charles Anderson, Pryor Blackwell and Thomas Leiser. The site cites developments and acquisitions 'in excess of 62 million square feet' (likely the partners' cumulative careers, not a dollar figure), so no USD scale is given. Bought the 1.1M-sq-ft Ross Tower and a three-building Preston Center portfolio in JVs with HPI Real Estate (and Second City Real Estate on Ross Tower).

firms.name: Billingsley Company
firms.notes: Founded 1978 by Lucy and Henry Billingsley; the firm says it builds, owns and manages its properties and publishes no portfolio dollar value. Employee count is Top Workplaces' '250 US Employees' (undated); other directories conflict (Built In lists 292; ZoomInfo a 51-200 band).

firms.name: Bridge Tower
firms.quote: more than 5,000 units in its portfolio or under construction
firms.notes: Dallas-based build-to-rent developer-operator co-founded in 2013 by managing partner Jackson Su; reported to have developed 24 BTR communities since 2016 and active in TX, NC, FL, GA and TN. Unit-count phrase comes via search summary of trade press; the firm's own website could not be reached. Name varies (Bridge Tower Group/Partners/Homes).

firms.name: Cawley Partners

Industrial division launched 2021 and has acquired 'nearly 6,000 acres in the DFW market'. A search summary attributed '$2.0 billion in transactions completed' and 11M+ sq ft to the company site, but I could not find it on any page I could load, so scale is left null.

No dollar-denominated scale figure was found, so value_usd is null (the scale entry records the acreage claim only). Legacy Hills is ~3,200 acres with 11,000+ planned units.

firms.name: Champion Partners
projects: Tradepoint East / 601 Distribution Drive (Wilmer, with Rosewood)

No firm-level dollar figure found; the $51M is a single Live Oak (San Antonio area) project cost from state filings, attribution to the CoStar link not verified line-by-line. Not plotted by size: the $51M is one project ($51M).

firms.name: Civitas Senior Living
projects: The Grandview of Chisholm Trail (Fort Worth)

firms.name: Dalfen Industrial
firms.quote: a portfolio exceeding 60 million square feet
firms.notes: Dallas-based buyer of infill last-mile industrial; portfolio stated in square feet (60M+ sf, June 2026), not dollars. Partnership with Goldman Sachs Alternatives; April 2026 bought a 1.4M sf DFW-heavy portfolio from Mapletree for $208M.

firms.name: Exxir Capital
firms.address: 101 North Zang Blvd, Suite 200, Dallas, TX 75208

No dollar scale published; founding year not found. Exxir sold a Bishop Arts retail/multifamily portfolio to Hines (JLL advised).

firms.name: Forestar Group
firms.quote: lot position at September 30, 2025 was 99,800 lots
firms.notes: Arlington-based residential lot developer (NYSE: FOR), majority-owned by D.R. Horton. Delivered more than 14,200 lots in fiscal 2025 and guided to $1.6-1.7 billion of revenue for fiscal 2026; 65,100 lots owned and 34,700 controlled.

firms.name: Gaedeke Group
firms.quote: three million square feet of Class A office properties
firms.notes: Family-owned Class A office investor headquartered in Dallas, led by CEO Sabine Gaedeke Stener; portfolio stated in square feet only. Founding year 1995 from a third-party listing.

firms.name: HALL Group
firms.notes: Founded 1968 by Craig Hall in Michigan; moved to Dallas in 1981; family-owned. The $7B figure is the projected value of the 162-acre HALL Park (Frisco) masterplan announced Oct 2021, a single-project pipeline figure, not AUM. Firm also runs HALL Structured Finance (lending), wineries and venture investing; no firmwide employee count found. Not plotted by size: the $7B is the HALL Park masterplan announced in 2021, not the firm ($7,000M).

Founded 1988 per company press materials (Gabriel Barbier-Mueller, founder/CEO); offices in Dallas, Geneva and London. In May 2025 it announced it was seeking capital partners to recapitalize. The preliminary 501-1000 employee band could not be verified (LinkedIn blocked) and would likely include restaurant/hotel staff.

firms.name: Hillwood
firms.notes: No published dollar AUM or portfolio value found; Hillwood reports scale in square feet, and figures conflict by scope (an Oct 2024 Hillwood release cites 31M SF industrial developed/acquired; third-party listings cite 230M+ SF developed globally). AllianceTexas is described as a '$120 billion economic engine' (economic impact, not company assets). Employee range is LinkedIn band seen in search results; other aggregators cite ~1,300, and DMN counted 412 local workers in 2017.

firms.name: Hoque Global
firms.notes: Mike Hoque's investment group; Dallas Innovates (2022) says it 'focuses on developing in underserved areas'. University Hills is a 270-acre plan next to UNT Dallas (1,500 multifamily units, 1.5M sq ft commercial, up to $31.4M TIF for phase one). No portfolio value or headcount published; 2007 founding and 1717 Main St. address come only from directory listings (a TDLR filing lists 1412 Main St.), so treat both as unconfirmed. The often-cited 300+ employees refers to Hoque's restaurant group DRG Concepts, not Hoque Global.

firms.name: Huffines Communities
firms.notes: Dallas master-planned community developer founded by Phillip and Donald Huffines; developed more than 10,000 homes across North Texas since 1985 (later reports say 15,000+ home sites). No dollar scale found; acreage figures vary across the company's own pages.

firms.name: Hunt Realty Investments
firms.notes: Real estate subsidiary of Hunt Consolidated, Inc.; site says 'For more than 50 years, Hunt Realty has been pursuing investments across Dallas and North Texas' but gives no founding year or portfolio value. No official headcount found (third-party estimates of 21-50 not used).

firms.name: Invitation Homes
firms.notes: Largest U.S. single-family rental REIT (NYSE: INVH); 110,187 homes owned and/or managed as of 30 Sep 2025 incl. JV and managed-only homes. Founded 2012 by Blackstone (founding year from general knowledge, unverified here).

firms.name: Jackson-Shaw

No company website, founding year or headcount found; TDLR filings give two different Plano addresses (5905 Legacy Dr.; 7200 Bishop Rd.), so HQ address left null. firms.notes: Real estate arm of the Hunt-family Rosewood Corporation; 'four decades' in real estate. Dec 2025 Atlanta purchase was its 85th self-storage facility (about 6 million sf across 23 states); closed a $125M refinance on a 19-property storage portfolio in May 2025. No firm-wide dollar AUM found.

firms.name: Skybox Datacenters
firms.notes: Dallas-based data center developer; PowerCampus Dallas is a JV with Bandera Ventures and Principal Asset Management. The $85M is the estimated cost of the first ~270,900 sf building only (as reported via search summary), not firm scale. Not plotted by size: the $85M is one building ($85M).

firms.name: Sonida Senior Living
firms.notes: Formerly Capital Senior Living (NYSE: SNDA). Owner-operator of senior housing; a pending merger with CNL Healthcare Properties (CHP) adds 69 communities in 2026. Employee estimates conflict widely across third-party sources, so left null. Address is from a directory listing.

firms.name: Stillwater Capital
firms.notes: No published firmwide AUM or portfolio value found; project-level figures include Haggard Farm, described by Bisnow (Dec 2025) as 'a $750M mixed-use project on the largest undeveloped site in Plano' with WoodHouse. Founding year 2010 comes from third-party listings (LoopNet), not the company site; offices also in Austin and Scottsdale.

firms.name: Trademark Property Company
firms.address: 1701 River Run, Suite 500, Fort Worth, TX 76107
firms.notes: Fort Worth-based mixed-use and retail developer; also has a Dallas office at 3800 Maple Ave. No firmwide AUM found; scale shown is only the construction loan for The Vickery, so it understates the firm. Took over management of Atlanta's Atlantic Station in 2026. Not plotted by size: the $61M is one loan ($61M).

firms.name: Trinsic Residential Group
firms.notes: Dallas multifamily developer (Aura brand). No dollar scale or founding year found on its site.

firms.name: WindMass Capital
firms.notes: Dallas value-add apartment syndicator led by Mitchell Voss; said in 2021 it held 29 communities and 7,100 units in North Texas. In March 2026 it faced foreclosure on a ~1,400-unit portfolio after an alleged default on a $120M Voya loan (scale figure is that debt, not AUM), and is in litigation with co-investor Fundamental. Flag as distressed. Not plotted by size: the $120M is one defaulted loan ($120M).
